\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Counter Prog Input: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CounterProgInput}.

\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Counter Prog Input: Results}

\begin{definition}[Shifting a counter-program input position]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.shiftInput}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.shiftInput}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.St}
Given a counter-program state $s$ and a natural number $n$, the shifted state has the
same label, register values, and output as $s$, while its input-read position is
increased by $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Indexed concatenation of lists]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.getElem?_append_length_add}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For any two bit lists $\mathrm{pre}$ and $\mathrm{suffix}$ and any $p\in\mathbb N$, the
element at index $|\mathrm{pre}|+p$ of their concatenation, if present, equals the
element at index $p$ of $\mathrm{suffix}$, if present.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Shifting the input by a prefix]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.step_shiftInput}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.step_shiftInput}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Instr, Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.getElem?_append_length_add, Complexity.CounterProg.shiftInput, Complexity.CounterProg.step}
\difficulty{5}
Let $R$ be the number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, and let $P$ assign
an instruction to each label. For any bit strings $\mathrm{pre}$ and $\mathrm{suffix}$
and any state $s$, taking one step on the concatenated input $\mathrm{pre} \mathbin{+\!\!+}\mathrm{suffix}$
from the state whose read position is increased by the length of
$\mathrm{pre}$ gives the same state as first taking one step on $\mathrm{suffix}$ from
$s$ and then increasing the resulting read position by the length of $\mathrm{pre}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Input-prefix shift invariance]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.run_shiftInput}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.run_shiftInput}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Instr, Complexity.CounterProg.St, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.run_succ, Complexity.CounterProg.shiftInput, Complexity.CounterProg.step_shiftInput}
\difficulty{4}
Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a set of labels, and let $P$ be a
counter program over them. For any bit strings $\mathrm{pre}$ and $\mathrm{suffix}$, any
abstract state $s$, and any $t\in\mathbb{N}$, running for $t$ steps on the concatenated
input $\mathrm{pre}\,\mathrm{suffix}$ from the state whose read position is shifted
forward by $|\mathrm{pre}|$ gives the state obtained by shifting the read position of
the $t$-step run on $\mathrm{suffix}$ from $s$ forward by $|\mathrm{pre}|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Prepending to the input]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.prepend_input}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes.prepend_input}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.Instr, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.run_shiftInput, Complexity.CounterProg.shiftInput}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ natural-number registers and labels in $\Lambda$,
let $u,v$ be binary strings, and suppose that on input $v$, every output word $o$ admits
a run of at most $b$ steps from label $\ell$, assignment $\rho$, and position $p$ to
label-or-halt state $\ell'$, assignment $\rho'$, and position $p'$, appending $e$. Then
on input $u$ followed by $v$, every $o$ admits a run of at most $b$ steps with the same
labels, assignments, and output extension, starting at position $|u|+p$ and ending at
position $|u|+p'$.
\end{theorem}
